approved: Social Services Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Bill 2015
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would make minor corrections and clarifications to several social security and family assistance laws.
It would change rules for special benefit, family tax benefit, student payments, and other social services to fix technical errors and remove ambiguities.
The amendments include aligning timeframes for family tax benefit reconciliation and changing how a new apprentice is defined in the Social Security Act.
Clarify that a person serving an income maintenance period for a mainstream payment cannot receive special benefit.
Align timeframes for meeting family tax benefit reconciliation conditions.
Alter the definition of 'new apprentice' to remove the need for a Commonwealth Registration Number and allow the Minister to set requirements by legislative instrument.
Confirm that only one course of education is considered when assessing full-time or qualifying study for student payments.
Clarify exemptions from the austudy assets test for people whose partner gets a relevant payment.
Simplify and consolidate indexation rules for pharmaceutical allowance and correct other technical errors.
People receiving or applying for social security payments and family tax benefit, including students, new apprentices, and those in financial hardship.

Labor supported the Social Services Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Bill 2015's minor housekeeping amendments, while opposing the government's cuts to family payments for 1.6 million families and three million children, paid parental leave, support for young unemployed, pensions, and the proposal to raise the retirement age to 70.

The bill makes technical amendments to social security and family assistance law, including clarifying that people serving an income maintenance period cannot access special benefit, reducing the timeframe for family tax benefit income reconciliation to one year, and removing the requirement for new apprentices to have a Commonwealth registration number.

A motion was moved requesting the Senate to resume consideration of 14 specified bills from the previous session, with each request to be conveyed in a separate message. The bills covered water amendment, managed investment trusts, social services, crime commission, deaths registration, tax and superannuation, crowd-sourced funding, firearms trafficking, and parliamentary entitlements.
